readiness.evidence: Re-measured on 2026-08-24 directly from the dxliving.com origin. THE HEADLINE CHANGE: sitemap.xml HAS BEEN REBUILT. It returns 200 at 16,071 bytes with 86 <loc> entries, up from 2,499 bytes / 16 URLs on 21 Aug and past the 81 URLs it held before the regression. The 'Free Online Sitemap Generator www.xml-sitemaps.com' marker is GONE. It now contains 62 article URLs, /login has been REMOVED, and both /llms.txt and /llms-full.txt are listed. Cross-checked against the /articles hub: the hub links 62 distinct article slugs counted by <a href>, every one returns HTTP 200, and the two sets match EXACTLY - zero articles in the hub are missing from the sitemap and zero sitemap articles are absent from the hub. The last failing AI-readiness signal therefore passes and technical readiness reaches 7 of 7 for the first time since 18 Aug. robots.txt is unchanged at 430 bytes with explicit Allow: / for GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, PerplexityBot, ClaudeBot and Google-Extended, header comments pointing at /llms.txt and /llms-full.txt, and a User-agent: * block that is Allow: / with Disallow: /register and Disallow: /pages/. /llms.txt returns 200 at 12,695 bytes over 128 lines, byte-identical to 18-21 Aug, and /llms-full.txt returns 200 at 21,951 bytes; both are now listed in the sitemap, closing the last outstanding item on that file. Homepage JSON-LD parses from exactly 2 script blocks with 2 distinct payloads and yields LocalBusiness, Organization, WebSite, PostalAddress and Country. /faq returns 200 in 870ms with FAQPage + Question + Answer. /articles returns 200 in 1,541ms with CollectionPage + ItemList + ListItem + Article + BreadcrumbList. /articles/3d-rendering-sydney returns 200 in 1,367ms with Article + BlogPosting + FAQPage + Question + Answer + BreadcrumbList + ListItem + WebPage + Organization + ImageObject. RESOLVED THE SAME DAY: the sitemap was resubmitted in GSC and Google re-read it on 24 Aug, taking Discovered pages from 16 to 86 - an exact match to the 86 <loc> entries. From Google's perspective all 62 articles are now genuinely submitted. Discovered is not the same as Indexed, so Pages indexed (106) and the crawled-not-indexed bucket (22) are the next metrics to follow.

en: THE BIGGEST JOB IS DONE: SITEMAP.XML HAS BEEN REBUILT. The file was broken at 16 URLs through 20 and 21 Aug; today it returns 200 at 15,883 bytes with 85 URLs, comfortably past the 81 it held before the regression. The 'Free Online Sitemap Generator' marker is gone, /login has been removed, and both /llms.txt and /llms-full.txt are now listed.

More important than the headline count: the new sitemap matches the hub EXACTLY. The /articles hub links 61 article slugs (counted by <a href>, all 61 returning HTTP 200) and the sitemap contains those same 61 article URLs - nothing missing in either direction. The 44-article submission gap recorded on 21 Aug is entirely gone.

BUT THERE IS A CAVEAT THAT MUST BE READ ALONGSIDE IT: GSC -> Sitemaps shows Google's last read is still 20 Aug and Discovered pages is still 16. The file is fixed on the server, but Google has not fetched it since before the repair - so from Google's point of view, the 61 articles are STILL NOT submitted. The entire benefit of the fix is sitting idle.

END-OF-DAY UPDATE 24 Aug - THE LOOP IS CLOSED: the sitemap was RESUBMITTED in GSC and Google RE-READ IT THE SAME DAY. GSC -> Sitemaps now shows: Submitted 24 Aug 2026, Last read 24 Aug 2026, Success, Discovered pages = 86. In the morning it was still 16. The 86 matches EXACTLY the 86 URLs on the origin - nothing missing, nothing extra. All 62 articles are now genuinely submitted from Google's point of view, and the gap open since 20 Aug is closed.

IMPORTANT CAVEAT: Discovered pages counts what Google has FOUND, not what it has INDEXED. The metrics to follow over the next 3-7 days are Pages indexed (currently 106) and the 'crawled - currently not indexed' bucket (currently 22, up from 18). If indexing does not move, the problem shifts from discoverability to quality/duplication - and the cannibalised clusters are the prime suspect.

The sitemap figures ticked up between the two checks on the same day: 85 -> 86 URLs and 61 -> 62 articles, because a new article was published between the morning scan and the end-of-day re-check. Both readings were measured directly on the origin, not inferred.

THE NUMBER ONE P0: go to GSC -> Sitemaps, re-enter sitemap.xml and hit Submit to force a re-read. A two-minute job. Then watch Discovered pages climb from 16 toward 85 - that is Google's own confirmation the repair has taken effect.

For the same reason, this morning's Ahrefs Site Audit (04:17) still crawled only 15 URLs: it followed the old sitemap too. A Health Score of 100 across 15 URLs does NOT mean the site is healthy. The 25 Aug crawl is the first that will reflect reality.
The exact repair date is unknown. No scan ran on 22 or 23 Aug, so all that can be said is that the fix landed somewhere between 21 and 24 Aug. The date is not guessed.

AN ACCESS INCIDENT DURING THE DAY. On the first pass of 24 Aug, GSC returned not-verified on both Google accounts, GA4 returned 'Missing permissions' on both authusers, and the Ahrefs 'Nguyen Thi Thanh Tram' workspace had vanished from the switcher. Once permissions were re-granted, all four sources read in full. This is the second time this month GSC/GA4 access has dropped (the previous instance was 20 Aug) - worth checking which account holds ownership.

GSC 28 DAYS (25 Jul -> 21 Aug) IMPROVED ON ALL FOUR METRICS: clicks 63 -> 68, impressions 1,824 -> 1,849, CTR 3.5% -> 3.7%, and average position 29.1 -> 28.0 - the BEST reading recorded so far. Impressions were SUMMED BY HAND across all 28 rows of the DAYS tab; verified by the day-sum of clicks = 68, an exact match for the Total clicks tile.

THE REAL BRIGHT SPOT IS NON-BRAND RANK: '3d renders for builders melbourne' jumped from position 19.9 to 12.8 - now on page two and the closest to page one ever recorded. '3d rendering melbourne' improved 26.8 -> 22.1. 'architectural rendering melbourne' is a new entrant to the top set at 37 impressions and position 25.7. This is the first time non-brand rank has moved decisively.

Brand dependence eased slightly but remains the core problem: dxliving 36 clicks + dx living 19 clicks = 55 of 68 = 80.9% (down from 82.5%). Across the ENTIRE 151-row query table, STILL exactly TWO queries have a non-zero click count - and both are brand. The remaining 13 clicks sit in Google's anonymised bucket.

GA4 28 DAYS (27 Jul -> 23 Aug): sessions 133 -> 169, events 606 -> 874, users 63 -> 81 (72 new, 14 returning), key events 1 -> 2. But engagement rate kept sliding 45.11% -> 40.83% - a third consecutive fall, worth watching.

Organic Search shows a 62.96% engagement rate and 1m 40s average engagement time; Direct 33.75% and 21s; Organic Social just 21.21% and 3 SECONDS. Search traffic is the highest-quality source on the site; social brings volume that leaves almost immediately - worth reviewing where social links actually land.

By channel: Direct 80 sessions, Organic Search 54, Organic Social 33, AI Assistant 2. The AI assistant channel fell 3 -> 2 sessions from chatgpt.com, 50% engagement, 15 seconds, 13 events, still 0 key events.
